Status 'construction': the detector is being assembled; sources through August 2026 say assembly and commissioning are still to be completed, and a November 2026 talk abstract plans stable data taking from January 2027 (planned interval, not an achieved milestone).
The muon-veto panels have been running in SUPL since 2024 (arXiv:2603.11981); this is the only SABRE South data published so far.

Conflict on the laboratory's own timeline (not edited here, the facility record is not owned by this stream): the SUPL page says the laboratory was officially unveiled in August 2022, the SABRE South papers say construction was completed in mid-2022 (arXiv:2211.03016), in 2023 (arXiv:2411.13889) and 'completed for first access in 2024' (arXiv:2511.16451).

physics_goals.quote: The SABRE South detector is designed to test the long-standing DAMA/LIBRA signal of an annually modulating rate consistent with dark matter by using the same target material.
physics_goals.value: Model-independent test of the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation with the same target material; the Southern Hemisphere location separates seasonal and site-related effects

summary.plain: SABRE South is the Australian half of a twin pair of sodium-iodide dark matter detectors, being assembled 1 km underground in the Stawell gold mine, Victoria. Being in the Southern Hemisphere helps tell a real dark matter signal from seasonal effects, when tested against DAMA/LIBRA's yearly signal. Its twin, SABRE North, is in Italy.
summary.technical: Seven ultra-high-purity NaI(Tl) crystals (35 kg or 50 kg in all) in oxygen-free copper enclosures, with Hamamatsu R11065 photomultipliers at both ends, suspended in an 11.6 kL linear alkylbenzene liquid-scintillator veto (at least 18 R5912 photomultipliers) inside steel and polyethylene shielding, with a muon veto of eight EJ-200 plastic scintillator panels. Expected background 0.72 cpd/kg/keV in 1-6 keV; 5 sigma discovery or 3 sigma exclusion of a DAMA/LIBRA-like modulation after two years. Muon flux at SUPL measured at (6.33 +- 0.04 +- 0.35) x 10^-8 cm^-2 s^-1 with the veto panels (2026).
